passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW We are a global leader in energy projects, technologies, systems, and services. We have manufacturing operations worldwide, strategically located to facilitate efficient delivery of these products, technologies, systems, and services to our customers. We report our results of operations in two segments: Subsea and Surface Technologies. Management’s determination of our reporting segments was made on the basis of our strategic priorities and corresponds to the manner in which our Chief Executive Officer reviews and evaluates operating performance to make decisions about resource allocations to each segment. A summarized description of our products and services and annual financial data for each segment can be found in Note 5 to our consolidated financial statements. 39 Total Company • Inbound orders of $11.2 billion drove backlog growth of 15% year-over-year to $16.6 billion; • Cash provided by operating activities increased 84% to $1.8 billion versus the prior year, with free cash flow growing 113% to $1.4 billion; • Shareholder distributions more than doubled versus the prior year—returning $1.0 billion through share repurchases and dividends—and authorized additional share repurchases of up to $2 billion; • Increased Company’s financial flexibility by reducing total short-term and long-term debt by $455.2 million while maintaining cash and cash equivalents above $1.0 billion; and • Reiterated our commitment to robust shareholder distributions, pledging to return at least 70% of free cash flow to shareholders in 2026. Subsea • Delivered on our commitment to achieve $30 billion in Subsea inbound orders over the 3-year period ending 2025, including $10.1 billion of orders in 2025; • Services inbound increased for a fifth consecutive year to more than $1.8 billion, supported by a growing installed base and aging infrastructure; • Combination of direct awards, iEPCI™ projects, and services exceeded 80% of Subsea inbound orders for the year, highlighting the strength of our differentiated offerings and innovative technologies; and • New iEPCI™ alliances with Vår Energi and Cairn Oil & Gas provide additional integrated opportunities. Surface Technologies • Inbound orders of $1.1 billion were driven by international markets; and • Revenue from international markets increased year-over-year, representing 65% of segment revenue; and • Experienced further commercial success of iComplete®—our high-performance, surface pressure containment ecosystem—with increased client adoption in high activity basins. We finished the year having delivered on many notable achievements. Importantly, these results reflect major milestones on our more ambitious journey ahead. We enter 2026 with a strong market outlook and a further step-up in our targeted financial performance. BUSINESS OUTLOOK Overall Outlook – The global economy is expected to show moderate growth in 2026, led by India, China, and the United States. Resilient consumer spending and easing of monetary policy in key regions should be essential drivers of economic growth. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Important risk factors that could impact our ability to achieve our anticipated operating results and growth plan goals are presented below. The following risk factors should be read in conjunction with discussions of our business and the factors affecting our business located elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in our other filings with the SEC. Summary Risk Factors The following is a summary of some of the risks and uncertainties that could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. You should read this summary together with the more detailed description of each risk factor contained below. Risks Related to Our Business and Industry • Demand for our products and services depends on oil and natural gas industry activity and expenditure levels and the demand for and price of oil and natural gas. • Competition and unanticipated changes relating to competitive factors in our industry, including ongoing industry consolidation, may impact our results of operations. 17 • Our success depends on our ability to develop, implement, and protect new technologies and services and intellectual property related thereto. • Cumulative loss of several major contracts, customers, alliances, or business disruptions may have an adverse effect on us. • Disruptions in the political, regulatory, economic, and social conditions or public health crises in the countries in which we conduct business, could adversely affect our business or results of operations. • Our existing and future debt may limit cash flows available to our operations and to service our outstanding debt. • A downgrade in our debt rating could restrict our ability to access financing. • Our acquisition and divestiture activities involve substantial risks. • Increasing scrutiny and expectations regarding sustainability matters could result in additional costs or risks or otherwise adversely affect our business. • Uncertainties with respect to the energy transition may adversely affect our business. Risks Related to Our Operations • We may lose money on fixed-price contracts. • Our failure to timely deliver our backlog could affect future sales, profitability, and customer relationships. • We face risks relating to our reliance on subcontractors, suppliers, and our joint venture partners. • A failure or breach of our IT infrastructure or that of our subcontractors, suppliers, or joint venture partners, including as a result of cyber-attacks, could adversely impact our business and results of operations. • We may use artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science in our business, and challenges with managing such technologies could adversely affect our business and results of operations. • Pirates and maritime conflicts endanger our maritime employees and assets. • Capital asset construction projects for vessels and manufacturing facilities are subject to risks, including delays and cost overruns. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers debt service comfortably, with free cash flow after capital expenditure exceeding reported debt by a wide margin. The company generated substantial cash from operations, reflecting strong conversion of earnings into cash and supporting internal funding of distributions and debt reduction.

The balance sheet holds a net cash position, with cash and cash equivalents exceeding total debt. Gross leverage is minimal and net leverage is negative, placing the company well below sector median leverage. Interest coverage is robust, with operating income covering interest expense many times over.

key_risks.text: Demand for the company's products and services depends on oil and natural gas industry activity and expenditure levels, and competition or industry consolidation may pressure results. These cyclical end-markets expose revenue and margins to commodity price swings and customer capital discipline, which could weaken cash generation and debt servicing capacity.

Debt maturities are concentrated in the near term, with a portion due within twelve months and a large balloon after year five. The company also maintains a revolving credit facility as a liquidity backstop for commercial paper. Refinancing risk is mitigated by cash balances and available commitments, but reliance on market access remains a consideration.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income covering interest expense many times over. This provides substantial headroom against earnings volatility. The company's minimal leverage and net cash position further reduce fixed charges relative to cash flow, supporting a very high debt servicing capacity.

Free cash flow to debt is very high, indicating that internally generated funds can retire debt rapidly. Operating cash flow increased significantly year over year, and capital expenditure remains modest relative to cash generation. This cash flow strength underpins the company's ability to meet maturities and return capital to shareholders.

overall_credit_view.text: The company exhibits a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with net cash, low leverage, and strong coverage. Operating performance has improved, with revenue and operating income rising over the past three years. These factors support a very strong credit profile relative to sector peers.

Shareholder distributions absorb a significant portion of free cash flow, with buybacks and dividends consuming most of the total. The company has committed to returning at least a majority of free cash flow to shareholders, which may limit deleveraging but is sustainable given current cash generation. Refinancing risk is manageable with ample liquidity.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋債務償付，扣除資本開支後之自由現金流大幅超過報告債務。公司從營運中產生大量現金，反映盈利轉化為現金之能力強勁，並支持以內部資金支付分派及減少債務。
資產負債表持有淨現金狀況，現金及現金等價物超過總債務。總槓桿極低，淨槓桿為負，使公司遠低於行業中位數槓桿。利息覆蓋率穩健，營運收入覆蓋利息支出多倍。

key_risks.text: 公司產品及服務之需求取決於石油及天然氣行業活動及支出水平，競爭或行業整合可能對業績構成壓力。該等週期性終端市場使收入及利潤率暴露於商品價格波動及客戶資本紀律，可能削弱現金產生及債務償付能力。
債務到期集中於短期，其中一部分於十二個月內到期，而五年後有大量氣球式還款。公司亦維持循環信貸融資作為商業票據之流動性後盾。再融資風險因現金結餘及可用承諾而減輕，但依賴市場准入仍為一項考慮因素。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，營運收入覆蓋利息支出多倍。這為盈利波動提供充足緩衝。公司極低之槓桿及淨現金狀況進一步降低相對於現金流之固定費用，支持極高之債務償付能力。
自由現金流對債務比率非常高，表明內部產生之資金可迅速償還債務。營運現金流按年顯著增加，而資本開支相對於現金產生仍屬溫和。此現金流實力支撐公司履行到期債務及向股東返還資本之能力。

overall_credit_view.text: 公司展現極低之指示性財務風險狀況，擁有淨現金、低槓桿及強勁覆蓋率。營運表現有所改善，過去三年收入及營運收入上升。該等因素支持相對於行業同業非常強勁之信用狀況。
股東分派佔自由現金流之顯著部分，回購及股息消耗總額之大部分。公司已承諾將至少大部分自由現金流返還股東，這可能限制去槓桿，但鑑於當前現金產生水平屬可持續。再融資風險因流動性充裕而可控。
